questions.q: What are the three stages of the SQL Server Database Administrator path, in order, per this lesson?
options: Job Ready, Advanced SQL Server, Multi-Platform Databases
Foundations, Intermediate, Expert
T-SQL, Azure, NoSQL
Beginner, Job Ready, Advanced
questions.explain: The path's three named stages are Job Ready, Advanced SQL Server, and Multi-Platform Databases.

questions.q: Which three courses make up the Job Ready stage of this path?
options: T-SQL Development, T-SQL for Database Administrators, SQL Server Database Administration
T-SQL Development, Azure Database Administrator, PowerShell Automation and DevOps for DBAs
SQL Server Performance Tuning, SQL Server HA Backup and Disaster Recovery, Azure Database Administrator
Cross-Platform Relational Database Administration, NoSQL Document and Graph Databases, T-SQL Development
questions.explain: Job Ready is T-SQL Development, T-SQL for Database Administrators, and SQL Server Database Administration, moving from writing SQL to administering it like a DBA.

questions.q: Where does the DP-300 certification sit in this path, per this lesson?
options: As a checkpoint at the end of the Advanced SQL Server stage, after Azure Database Administrator — not the end of the path
It is the very first thing covered, before any T-SQL content
It is earned only after completing all nine courses
It has no connection to any course in this path
questions.explain: The lesson places DP-300 as a checkpoint at the end of Stage 2 (Advanced SQL Server), tied to the Azure Database Administrator course — explicitly not the path's conclusion.

questions.q: Which two courses make up the Multi-Platform Databases stage that this course belongs to?
options: Cross-Platform Relational Database Administration and NoSQL, Document & Graph Databases
Azure Database Administrator and PowerShell, Automation & DevOps for DBAs
SQL Server Performance Tuning and SQL Server HA, Backup & Disaster Recovery
T-SQL Development and T-SQL for Database Administrators
questions.explain: Stage 3, Multi-Platform Databases, consists of Cross-Platform Relational Database Administration and this course, NoSQL, Document & Graph Databases.

questions.q: According to this lesson's honest career framing, where does NoSQL/multi-model skill actually pay off for a DBA?
options: As a real, differentiating specialization at companies running polyglot-persistence architectures — not as a universal requirement for every DBA role
It is required for every DBA job posting from this point forward
It replaces the need for SQL Server skills entirely
It only matters for companies that have fully abandoned relational databases
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit: this skill is genuinely valuable and differentiating in polyglot-persistence environments, which are increasingly common but not universal — it does not make relational skill optional or obsolete.
